incidents.title: LifeTouch Health reports unauthorized access to patient information
incidents.summary: LifeTouch Health, formerly Arkansas Hospice, said an intruder accessed information on its network between February 25 and March 12. It reported 38,629 affected people to HHS. The company did not confirm that files were copied; potentially exposed data varied by patient.
match: Data Breaches Announced by LifeTouch Health
LifeTouch Health and MPOWERHealth Disclose Network Intrusions

sources.label: LifeTouch’s October 12 notice filed in Massachusetts
HHS Office for Civil Rights breach portal
The HIPAA Journal’s coverage of the notices

affected: LifeTouch Health patients. Potentially exposed data included treatment or diagnosis details, financial or identity information, and insurance information.
payloads: LifeTouch detected suspicious network activity after some systems became unavailable. Its notice did not disclose an initial access method.
guidance: Check your notification for the offered identity-protection services and review account statements, credit reports, and explanations of benefits.

incidents.title: Gyazo breach affected 23.62 million account records and image metadata
incidents.summary: Helpfeel reported that an intrusion into Gyazo affected about 23.62 million account records, not that many unique people, and hundreds of millions of image metadata records. Forensics confirmed that 432 image files belonging to 133 users were viewed or obtained, but found no evidence of large-scale acquisition of image files. The logs did not identify exactly which records were transferred.
match: Gyazo account and image metadata incident

sources.label: Helpfeel’s final report and November 5 correction

updates.text: Helpfeel added about 174 million metadata records for deleted images to the disclosed scope; this did not mean those image files were taken.
Gyazo resumed service after security checks and other countermeasures.
Final forensics confirmed that 432 files belonging to 133 Gyazo users were viewed or obtained. Logs did not establish the exact contents of the outbound transfer.
Helpfeel corrected the scope of deleted-image metadata to about 1.12 million associated accounts. The 174 million figure counts metadata records, not accounts or image files.

affected: Gyazo account data, including about 5.62 million records linked to registered email addresses and about 18.01 million anonymous account records.
Separate image metadata sets included records for deleted images. Helpfeel did not find evidence that the corresponding deleted image files were acquired.
payloads: An intrusion through Gyazo’s image upload server led to database access. Investigators observed large database reads and an outbound transfer, but logs did not capture its contents.
Helpfeel reported exposure of password hashes, not plaintext passwords, and did not confirm exposure of payment information.
guidance: Reset your Gyazo password if you have not already done so. Change reused passwords on other services and review older images before restoring their sharing access.
For workplace accounts, review older screenshots for credentials or other secrets. Revoke exposed secrets and review sign-in and integration activity.
